Priya: Heads-up — long-running Qwen-32k inference jobs show steady KV memory growth even after warmup. Not a single huge spike, just linear climb over ~10k extra tokens :thinking_face:
Priya: Repro: run with `--model qwen-32k`, `--rope-scaling auto`, `--kv-mode gqa`, small batch (1) and steady streaming requests.
Priya: Profiler snippet:
```
KV pages: 12.3GB @ 40k tokens
KV pages: 14.1GB @ 50k tokens
KV pages: 16.9GB @ 60k tokens
KV pages: 18.7GB @ 70k tokens
(allocs are mostly 'partial page' fragments)
```
Sam: ack. does this happen on both kernel-auto and kernel=fast paths?
Priya: I tried kernel=auto (default) and kernel=fast — both climb, but auto climbs ~10% faster.
Sam: hmm. which quantization path? mqa or gqa?
Priya: gqa enabled; we have a separate mqa job that doesn't show the same slope (needs longer run to be sure).
Alex: @Priya can you grab `kv.page_map` snapshot + `slab` histogram from the same run? I suspect fragmentation: partial pages accumulating because rope-scaled key sizes don't match page slots.
Priya: pasted small dump (trimmed):
```
page_map: [used: 8132, free_fragments: 2174, avg_fragment_bytes: 3.1k]
slab: {8K: 1200, 16K: 400, 64K: 34}
kv_residency: mean=0.72, tail95=0.98
```
Rachel: that avg_fragment_bytes looks high for qwen rope-scaling. In a past Mistral case we saw rope factor mismatch causing lots of partial-page allocations — turned out to be kernel-side rounding behavior when switching kernels mid-epoch.
Alex: exactly. my theory: kernel-auto is switching kernels based on sequence-length distribution, and kernel switch changes key packing/align semantics. pages already allocated stay in older format -> cannot be coalesced -> fragmentation.
Sam: can you repro with `--kernel-lock` to force single kernel for whole run? if growth stops, we can blame kernel-switch.
Priya: will run with `--kernel-lock=fast` and `--kernel-lock=slow` tomorrow and post results.
infra-bot: kv-gc job started on cluster-7 at 2026-03-17T22:12:01Z (job id kv-gc-2310008) :gear:
Sam: another angle: check prefix/KV reuse heuristics. if prefix cache misses cause re-inserts slightly different sizes (rope scaling rounding) you'll see growth. add logs for `kv.insert_size` and `kv.lookup_shape` for the run.
Priya: adding those metrics. quick peek shows `kv.insert_size` toggling between 4096 and 8192 for same prompt family when sequence grows past rope boundaries.
Rachel: that's the smoking gun. Qwen's rope scaling reports a fractional scale for attention that we round differently across kernels (gqa vs mqa path). when one insert uses 4K and later a 8K allocation is made for same key, old 4K fragment remains -> fragmentation.
Alex: mitigation options: 1) unify rounding (fast) 2) force coalescing/compaction in kv-gc (expensive) 3) prefer fixed kernel per route.
Sam: for the short term, try kernel-lock + disable rope-scaling auto on one canary feed. if stable, roll fix to kernel selection heuristic to prefer stability over micro throughput gains.
Priya: running two canaries now: canary-A (kernel-lock=fast, rope-scaling=off), canary-B (kernel-lock=auto, rope-scaling=auto). will report in ~4h.
Priya: also opened a small perf trace with `--kv-debug` and uploaded to /tmp/qwen-kv-trace-2310009999.log (link: https://internal.redwood/p/qwen-kv-trace-2310009999)
Alex: ping me when traces are up. I'll try a local sim to test fragmentation coalescing logic.
Rachel: filing a follow-up bug to check kernel packing math for GQA vs MQA, tagging runtime and ml-inference.
Sam: nice investigative work. if canary-A holds, we should consider rolling kernel-lock for hotspot routes until we fix rounding.
Priya: thanks — will update thread after canary. :thumbsup:
